title: Navimower 0.4.4-beta30

## Mowing pause reason status

This beta adds a dedicated Home Assistant status sensor for retained mowing interruptions, with conservative low-battery confirmation intended for automations.

### New `Mowing pause reason` sensor

The sensor reports the current retained-task interruption as one of the observed semantic states, including:

- `none` — no retained mowing interruption is currently attributed;
- `low_battery_pending` — Navimower observed an unfinished Mowing -> Returning/Docked transition at or below the configured return-battery threshold, after excluding known Home Assistant Dock, night and schedule-window stop cases, but the vendor feed has not yet confirmed the cause;
- `low_battery` — the same low-battery candidate is additionally confirmed by a time-matched vendor Device notification with code `1502`;
- `night` — the retained task was attributed to the existing night-mowing/sunset pause logic;
- `manual_dock` — Home Assistant explicitly sent Dock;
- `unknown` — the interruption could not be safely attributed.

The entity includes useful attributes such as pause confidence, progress and battery before the pause, configured return-battery level, pause timestamp, task origin/trigger and vendor confirmation metadata.

### Conservative automation semantics

Generic mower state values are not treated as proof of a low-battery pause. `Paused`, `Returning` and `Docked` are cause-agnostic states and may also occur for manual Dock, night mowing rules or other situations.

For that reason:

- `low_battery_pending` is intentionally **not** marked automation-safe;
- `low_battery` requires the existing low-battery transition attribution **and** a matching vendor `1502` notification within five minutes of the observed pause;
- an old/unrelated `1502` notification cannot confirm a newer pause;
- unrelated vendor notification codes cannot confirm the state.

For conservative automations, trigger on `sensor.<mower>_mowing_pause_reason` changing to `low_battery`. The vendor notification feed is rate-limited to a 60-second refresh interval, so confirmed status can appear after the mower has already begun returning/charging; `low_battery_pending` provides the earlier inferred status for users who deliberately prefer faster but less certain behavior.
